title: Co-ordination and Controlling
summary: Co-ordination is the orderly arrangement of individual and group efforts to provide unity of action in the pursuit of a common goal. It harmonises the activities of different departments (purchase, production and marketing) so that planned objectives are achieved with minimum conflict. Brech: balancing and keeping together the team by ensuring suitable allocation of tasks and harmony among members. Characteristics: it integrates group efforts, ensures unity of action, is a continuous process, all pervasive (a function of managers in all departments and at all levels), is the responsibility of all managers and is a deliberate function. It is called the 'essence' of management.

Significance (increasing with size): growth in size and volume of work means more people and groups working at cross purposes; activities located at different places do not permit close interaction; functional differentiation, division and sub-division of activities and specialisation make co-ordination both more difficult and more important. It helps in reconciliation of goals, total accomplishment of objectives, harmonious relationships and economy and efficiency.

Controlling is evaluating actual performance against planned or standard performance and taking corrective action if necessary. Henri Fayol: 'Control consists in verifying whether everything occurs in conformity with the plan adopted, the instructions issued and principles established.' It includes quality, time and cost, not only quantity. Characteristics: control is a function of management and depends on planning (planning precedes controlling); a continuous process; all pervasive; action is the essence of control; forward looking.

Why control is needed: helps in achieving targets, taking corrective action on time, monitoring and improving employee performance, achieving better coordination and better planning, minimising errors, facilitating decision making and simplifying supervision. Relationship between planning and controlling: planning fixes the goals or standards and controlling checks actual performance with them; without planning control is blind and planning is fruitful only when control is exercised; planning is forward looking (and uses past data) while control is backward looking (compares past performance) as well as forward looking; control brings out shortcomings of planning.

Steps: (1) establishment of standards (quantitative, realistic and attainable, with a range of tolerable deviations); (2) measurement of performance (observation, inspection, reports); (3) comparison of actual performance with standards (equal, more or less); (4) detecting the reasons for deviations; (5) taking corrective action (revision of standards, better selection and training, better motivation) for major deviations outside the permissible range.

Which function ensures the right timing and sequence of activities?

objective: Fill in the blanks: (a) Control looks back at ______ performance. (b) Control looks forward to ______ performance.
Identify the management function: (a) Ensures the right timing and sequence of activities. (b) Ensures that activities conform to the plans.
State true or false: (i) Co-ordination leads to diversity in action. (ii) Control is a continuous process.
Name any two features of control.
It is a continuous process; it is all pervasive and action oriented (any two).
Arrange the steps of the control process: comparing actual performance, setting standards, corrective action, measuring performance, finding reasons for deviation.
Setting standards; measuring performance; comparing performance with standards; finding reasons for deviation; corrective action.
Fill in the blanks: Planning fixes the ______ and controlling checks the ______ performance against them.
State true or false: (i) Without planning control is blind. (ii) Minor deviations within the permissible range need major corrective action.
Name the management function called the 'essence of management'.
vsa: A car company's sales team promised early delivery but production could not meet it. Which management function is missing? Mention two problems.
Co-ordination; customer dissatisfaction and a decline in the company's reputation.
What is meant by controlling? Name its first step.
Controlling is evaluating actual performance against standards and taking corrective action; first step: establishment of standards.
Why is co-ordination called the essence of management?
Because all functions need unity of action and co-ordination ties departments and efforts together to reach common goals.
State any two characteristics of co-ordination.
It integrates group efforts and is a continuous and all-pervasive process.
How does a deviation within the permissible range get treated?
No corrective action is needed; managers act only on major deviations outside the range.
State any two limitations of standards in control.
If too high, employees are discouraged; if too low, efficiency falls and costs rise.
sa: A factory manager regularly checks the production output and compares it with the daily target. Explain how this illustrates the controlling function.
He measures actual output, compares it with the standard (daily target), finds deviations, ascertains reasons and takes corrective action, which are the steps of controlling.
Explain any three points of significance of co-ordination.
It reconciles goals of different departments, avoids overlapping and conflict as size grows and ensures economy and efficiency.
Explain any three characteristics of co-ordination.
It integrates group efforts, ensures unity of action and is continuous, all pervasive and the responsibility of all managers.
Explain the importance of controlling (any three points).
Helps in achieving targets, takes corrective action on time and improves employee performance.
Explain the process of control in three steps (any three).
Setting standards, measuring actual performance and comparing it with standards.
la: Establishing standards, measuring performance, comparing it with standards, detecting reasons for deviations and taking corrective action.
Explain the importance of co-ordination and why it is called the essence of management.
As size, location and specialisation increase, co-ordination gives unity of action, reconciles goals and brings efficiency and harmony.
Explain why control is needed and its characteristics.
Control helps achieve targets and corrective action on time, improves performance, coordination and planning; it is continuous, all-pervasive, action-oriented and forward looking.
